data.cultural_impact: The name Muayyid in Islamic culture holds a significant meaning as it denotes a person who offers aid and assists others in their time of need. This name is often given to a child to encourage a sense of responsibility, kindness, and compassion towards others. Muayyid is a reminder that being helpful and supportive to those around us is a crucial part of building strong community bonds, and is highly valued in Islamic society.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Muayyid holds a deeper meaning as it signifies one who actively participates in the support and guidance of others on their spiritual journey. Understanding the significance of helping others in their faith and personal growth, a Muayyid is encouraged to share their knowledge and wisdom with others, acting as a mentor or guide. In doing so, they not only help others grow spiritually but also deepen their own connection to Allah, as they engage in acts of kindness and charity.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'Muqaddimah' mentions Muayyid al-Din al-Shirazi as the founder of the Hafsid dynasty in Ifriqiya (modern-day Tunisia) in 894 A.D. under the Aghlabid rule.
historical_references.context: Muayyid al-Din was a Berber tribal chief who seized power from the Aghlabid rulers and established the Hafsid dynasty, becoming its first ruler.

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi's 'Kitab al-Mawāʿiẓ wa-l-Iʿtibār bi-Dhayl ʿIlā al-Taʿrīkh' records Muayyid al-Din Biyabagh as a military commander who served under the Ayyubid ruler Saladin and played a crucial role in the Battle of Hattin (1119 A.D.) against the Crusaders.
historical_references.context: Muayyid al-Din Biyabagh was a Muslim general who led a successful charge against the Crusader forces at the Battle of Hattin, turning the tide of the battle in favor of Saladin.
